pots.title: What Is Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome?
pots.excerpt: This JAMA Patient Page describes who is typically affected by postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, the risk factors, and the diagnosis and treatment.

pots.title: Antidepressants in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS): A scoping review.
pots.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
pots.authors: Blitshteyn, Svetlana, Reiersen, Angela M, Weinstock, Leonard B, Speed, Traci J et al.
pots.excerpt: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is one of the most common autonomic disorders with increasing prevalence and incidence after COVID-19 pandemic. Despite standard treatment of POTS consisting of nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic therapies that decrease heart rate and increase blood pressure and plasma volume, antidepressant medications are widely utilized in patients with POTS.

mcas.title: IL-17Rb mediates the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis through STAT6-dependent regulation of TH2 cells and type 2 inflammatory cytokines.
mcas.authors: Wei, Meng-Yi, Liu, Zheng, Chen, Qi, Li, Hao et al.
mcas.excerpt: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear.

mcas.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pro-tumorigenic intestinal mast cell programs in colorectal cancer.
mcas.authors: Putro, Erisa, Carnevale, Alessia, Marangio, Caterina, Pietropaolo, Giuseppe et al.
mcas.excerpt: Mast cells (MCs) are multifunctional immune cells with context-dependent functions in cancer. In colorectal cancer (CRC), their contribution remains debated, suggesting that distinct MC subsets may either support tumor progression or promote anti-tumor immunity.

mcas.title: Environmental Ligands of the Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor in Allergic Rhinitis: Immune and Neuroimmune Mechanisms.
mcas.authors: Xiong, Yalan, Han, Jia, Yang, Zhaoxin, Liu, Yongqin et al.
mcas.excerpt: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is an immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated chronic inflammatory disease. Although type 2 immune responses are central to AR, environmental exposures, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions also contribute to disease development.

mcas.title: Comorbidities in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria: Integrating Disease Drivers and Systemic Consequences.
mcas.authors: Kim, Joo-Hee, Kim, Mi-Ae, Ye, Young-Min
mcas.excerpt: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a mast cell-driven inflammatory skin disorder traditionally considered self-limiting and non-life-threatening. However, accumulating evidence suggests that CSU is associated with multiple comorbidities, reflecting systemic immune and neuroinflammatory dysregulation.

mcas.title: Candidate biomarkers predicting clinical outcome after hyperbaric oxygen against chronic radiation cystitis.
mcas.authors: Giglio, Daniel, Sallam, Lana, Thorsell, Annika, Mölne, Johan et al.
mcas.excerpt: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) is effective against radiation cystitis. In this exploratory analysis we employed proteomics to assess biomarkers predicting clinical efficacy and the pharmacodynamics of HBO2 in radiation cystitis.

mcas.authors: Van Zyl, Werner Richardt, Henning, Sanchen

mcas.title: Sex differences in the effect of viable cell-containing and heat-killed Roseburia faecis on repeated water avoidance stress-induced irritable bowel syndrome Wistar rat model.
mcas.authors: Ha, Sungchan, Kim, Nayoung, Nam, Ryoung Hee, Jin, Isom et al.
mcas.excerpt: Roseburia faecis has been reported to mitigate irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), which is characterized by altered intestinal motility, mucosal immune activation, and gut microbial dysbiosis. This study aimed to evaluate the sex-dependent effects of heat-killed R. faecis (HK-BBH024) and a viable cell-containing R. faecis preparation (L-BBH024) in a repeated water avoidance stress (rWAS)-induced IBS Wistar rat model.

mcas.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
mcas.authors: Song, Xiaowen, Liu, Xuexin, Yang, Le, Yan, Guangli et al.
mcas.excerpt: The systemic and relapsing nature of urticaria cannot be fully explained by cutaneous mast-cell activation alone. Whether the gut contributes, and whether a multi-component formula such as Jingfang Mixture (JF) acts through a gut-skin route, have not been tested together at the level of microbiota, metabolites, and skin signaling together.

mcas.excerpt: Food allergy (FA) pathogenesis is closely associated with perturbations of the enteric ecosystem; however, comparative studies examining how distinct allergen triggers differentially affect the enteric mycobiome (total fungal community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) and the enteric bacteriome (total bacterial community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) remain limited. Mapping these allergen-specific...

mcas.title: A progressive ODE model of seasonal allergic rhinitis: from core Th2 axis to 21-dimensional multi- pathway integration with seasonal dynamics and directional assessment.
mcas.authors: Zhang, Qiang, Hu, Houyang, Yue, Yi, Qi, Wenwen et al.
mcas.excerpt: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (SAR) affects approximately 400 million individuals worldwide, yet a quantitative framework integrating the complete immunological cascade from allergen exposure to clinical symptoms is lacking. Individual pathways (Th2/IgE, TLR4/NF-κB, Th17/Treg) have been characterized in isolation, but their interactions and relative contributions to symptom generation remain poorly understood.

mcas.title: The potential therapeutic efficacy of platelet-rich plasma gel on experimentally induced localized scleroderma in adult male albino rats.
mcas.authors: El-Shafei, Asmaa Ahmed, Hosny, Sara Adel, El Sayed, Hagar, Mohamed, Hala Hassan
mcas.excerpt: Localized scleroderma, or morphea, is an autoimmune fibrotic disorder characterized by dermal or deeper tissue inflammation and excessive collagen deposition, leading to skin thickening, sclerosis, and eventual atrophy. Early diagnosis is essential to prevent permanent cosmetic and functional impairment.

mcas.title: Surface Chemistry Governs Early Redox and Cytokine Responses to Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide Nanoparticles Across Hepatic-Relevant Cell Models.
mcas.authors: Heaton, Bethany J, Sikora, Aneta, Bartczak, Dorota, Goenaga-Infante, Heidi et al.
mcas.excerpt: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are increasingly utilised in biomedical and nanomedicine applications, raising important questions regarding early interactions with hepatic cellular systems. This study investigated how surface chemistry influences the biological behaviour of SPIONs across hepatic-relevant cell models through integrated physicochemical characterisation and response screening.

mcas.title: Probiotic
mcas.authors: Qiu, Jingcheng, Chen, Zhouhua, Chen, Tao, Cao, Lu
mcas.excerpt: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU)-induced oral mucositis (OM) is associated with the fat-tissue-associated protein (FTO)/cytidine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2)/NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammatory axis. A hamster OM model was established using 5-FU injections and mechanical irritation, with LR administered in drinking water.

mcas.title: Development of a Mast-Cell Activation Test for Diagnosing Allergic Rhinitis.
mcas.authors: Pan, Jianli, Gong, Ling, Xu, Jie, Luo, Shiqiong et al.
mcas.excerpt: Serum-specific IgE (sIgE) and skin prick testing (SPT) have limitations in diagnosing allergic rhinitis (AR). CD63, a mast cell activation biomarker reflecting degranulation extent, has unclear application in AR diagnosis.

mcas.title: CD63 aptamer-based electrochemical sensor assesses stored red blood cell-derived exosome burden associated with mast-cell-mediated transfusion-related acute lung injury.
mcas.authors: Zheng, Ling, Su, Shan-Shan, Qin, Sai-Nan, Ren, Yimin et al.
mcas.excerpt: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) remains a serious complication of transfusion, and blood component-derived exosomes have been proposed as candidate contributors to transfusion-related inflammatory dysregulation. Rapid and practical methods to assess exosome burden in stored red blood cell (RBC) units remain limited.

other-post-viral.title: Acute Zonal Occult Outer Retinopathy: Reappraising a Historical Clinical Concept in the Era of Multimodal Imaging.
other-post-viral.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
other-post-viral.authors: Ramtohul, Prithvi, Fouad, Yousef, Bianco, Lorenzo, Feo, Alessandro et al.
other-post-viral.excerpt: Acute zonal occult outer retinopathy (AZOOR) and the broader "AZOOR complex" have historically encompassed several disorders sharing acute visual symptoms and outer retinal dysfunction. Advances in multimodal imaging have revealed structural abnormalities in many of these presentations, challenging the original concept of an "occult" retinopathy without a visible anatomical correlate.
